segments.speaker: corvin_ashby
segments.text: Forty years of goblin trade in the ledgers, and we ended it in a morning. I'm writing that down.

segments.speaker: corvin_ashby
segments.text: The clan keeps songs older than my oldest page. I've begged for a copy. Twice.

segments.speaker: corvin_ashby
segments.text: You found it. The ember. May I... no. No, don't hand it to me. I'd only want to know what it costs.

segments.speaker: corvin_ashby
segments.text: I've written down the bridge. All of it. Someone should, while we still remember it right.

segments.speaker: corvin_ashby
segments.text: Mother Skarrow's people remember things my ledgers don't. If you go up the hill again, ask them about the seven. Please.

segments.speaker: mother_aubrine
segments.text: I said the rites for everyone who died at the ford. All of them. The gods can sort out whose they were.

segments.speaker: mother_aubrine
segments.text: Goblin children came to my door asking what the bell is for. I had no idea what to tell them.

segments.speaker: mother_aubrine
segments.text: Something under the river kept us warm, and now you carry it. Tell me plainly. Is it the gods' gift, or someone's theft?

segments.speaker: mother_aubrine
segments.text: I prayed for the dead at the ford this morning. All of them. Forgive me if I prayed for you as well.

segments.speaker: mother_aubrine
segments.text: The clan's children came to my door asking about the bell. I told them it rings for supper. Now it does.
